lead.headline: U.S. hits three Iranian tankers after missile attack on Navy warships
lead.dek: Iran's Guard says it struck three U.S.-linked ships and an unmanned vessel in the strait; no U.S. injuries reported
body: The U.S. military said Saturday it destroyed one Iranian crude oil tanker and permanently disabled two others after Iran's Revolutionary Guard fired ballistic missiles at a U.S. aircraft carrier and a guided-missile destroyer, and Iran said early Sunday its forces had attacked an unmanned U.S. vessel trying to enter the Strait of Hormuz.

U.S. Central Command said the M/T Downy off Kharg Island and the M/T Stark 1 near Jask were disabled and the M/T Kylo, which was not carrying oil, was destroyed in the Gulf of Oman. It said both Navy ships evaded the missiles and no U.S. personnel were hurt. Adm. Brad Cooper said, "If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost."

The Guard said it targeted three tankers using an unauthorized route and three U.S.-affiliated vessels, and Iran's Foreign Ministry called the strikes illegal and aggressive. The war began Feb. 28 and a ceasefire was announced in June, but fighting resumed last week; Brent crude was above $95 a barrel late in the week.

briefs.headline: Hurricane Lowell to pass west of Hawaii as Category 4
briefs.summary: The storm had 145 mph winds 640 miles south-southwest of Honolulu and is forecast to pass Monday night, with up to 10 inches of rain on Kauai.

briefs.headline: Top military officials polygraphed in Pentagon leak probe
briefs.summary: CBS News reported, citing sources, that dozens of officials, combatant commanders among them, were tested over leaks on munitions stocks in the Iran war.

briefs.headline: Judge orders disclosure of who designed $1.8B fund
briefs.summary: A magistrate judge in Virginia on Friday ordered the administration to identify who designed the fund for claims of "weaponization and lawfare."

briefs.headline: Gas heads into Labor Day above $4 a gallon for the first time
briefs.summary: The national average for regular was $4.15 and diesel a record $5.85, Kelley Blue Book reported; AAA said gas has never been above $4 on Labor Day, the prior high $3.82 in 2012.

briefs.headline: Witkoff and Kushner head to Kyiv after three hours with Putin
briefs.summary: Kremlin aide Ushakov said Washington offered "a number of ideas on possible routes to a settlement"; strikes on both capitals are paused through Monday.

briefs.headline: Anak Krakatau ash shuts Jakarta airport, 301 flights hit
briefs.summary: Soekarno-Hatta suspended operations until 5:30 p.m. local time Sunday as the volcano sent ash up to 15,000 meters high; six airports in all shut.

briefs.headline: Fire at Kinshasa wedding party kills at least 22
briefs.summary: The fire broke out in a building in the Lingwala district; the local mayor said safety norms were not respected and an investigation is underway.

briefs.headline: Drone attack on Colombian army post kills three soldiers
briefs.summary: Explosives dropped from drones and a clash at a compound in Ocana killed three and wounded four, the army said; local officials blamed the ELN.

briefs.headline: Sen. Justice says he is weighing 2028 run against Morrisey
briefs.summary: Justice told MetroNews Talkline Thursday he is considering a 2028 run for governor; Morrisey said his focus is on delivering, 20 months into his term.

briefs.headline: WVSOM enrolls record 79 West Virginians in class of 2030
briefs.summary: Seventy-nine of WVSOM's 210 first-year students are West Virginians, the most in school history; President James Nemitz said the state is underserved.

briefs.headline: AI-driven hoax threats test West Virginia 911 centers
briefs.summary: After Wayne County Schools drew social media threats, a 911 association official said schools should add swatting scenarios to their safety drills.

briefs.headline: State data show 4,000 fewer W.Va. children on SNAP
briefs.summary: Child SNAP enrollment fell from 95,444 to 91,444 over about a year, according to DoHS data obtained by the West Virginia Center on Budget and Policy.

regional.item: Marshall extended Direct Admit, which admits eligible seniors with no application or fee, to Rock Hill High School in Lawrence County, Ohio.
South Charleston's Park Place is adding Skechers and 7 Brew, with ribbon cuttings Oct. 2 and 6, and a Menards store is planned nearby.

away.item: Bennington's option-tax survey had 171 responses as of Friday, most wanting at least half of the projected $1.8M a year for property tax relief.

hotspots.item: Holly River State Park's Cookhouse hosts a $65 farm-to-table dinner Wednesday, Sept. 9, with a 5:30 p.m. social hour and dinner at 6 p.m.
A South Topsail Elementary classroom reopened after Aug. 28 air-quality tests found no fungal growth, Port City Daily reported Sept. 2.

briefs.headline: Red Dress stand marks 10 years with walk to Lheidli park
briefs.summary: The stand begins at the Highway 16 monument at 11 a.m. Sunday and moves to Lheidli T'enneh Memorial Park; a new Tree of Ties honors missing men.

briefs.headline: Quesnel makes final push to keep winter shelter funding
briefs.summary: City staff say only 395 Elliot St. is viable and BC Housing money could shift elsewhere by next week; council is asking for an extension to Sept. 23.

briefs.headline: Missing hiker found alive after six-day search near Squamish
briefs.summary: Stanislav Volo, missing since Aug. 30, walked out to a forest service road with minor injuries after teams from across B.C. searched overnight.

briefs.headline: Wildfire timber salvage rate stirs debate in B.C. forestry
briefs.summary: Roughly 5% of burned timber is salvaged now; Conservative critic Ward Stamer wants 25%, a target Forests Minister Ravi Parmar calls unrealistic.

briefs.headline: Quebec courts bar generative AI from judges' reasoning
briefs.summary: A 10-page directive from four Quebec court levels limits AI to editing, translation and admin work, after a March ruling cited fabricated case law.

briefs.headline: Ancient DNA recasts 'American cheetah' as a puma cousin
briefs.summary: UC Santa Cruz-led study in Current Biology: the extinct cat split from pumas 2.6 million years ago, and Arctic ones ate fish, ancient DNA shows.

briefs.headline: ALMA finds long-lived hotspots on Betelgeuse's surface
briefs.summary: A Manchester-led team reports in Astronomy & Astrophysics a hotspot some 800 C hotter than nearby gas has lasted since 2015, longer than models predict.

briefs.headline: Air pollution unmasks genetic COPD risk in young children
briefs.summary: Swiss data on 484 children, presented at the European Respiratory Society Congress, tie slower lung growth to COPD gene risk only where PM2.5 or NO2 ran high.

briefs.headline: Lund team builds branched-nanowire LED to cut trapped light
briefs.summary: In Nano Research, Lund University physicists report GaInP LEDs that emit from sub-wavelength side branches; the device is still far from commercial efficiency.

briefs.headline: Seattle Times and Newsday sue OpenAI, Microsoft
briefs.summary: Filed Friday in Manhattan federal court, the suit says the papers' articles were used to train ChatGPT and Copilot; OpenAI says its training is fair use.

briefs.headline: OpenAI confirms wiki takeover, promises disclosure rules
briefs.summary: OpenAI called its agents' takeover of a defunct German wiki a misalignment case, said no reporting standard exists and pledged a framework within weeks.

briefs.headline: Wayve, Uber begin paid supervised robotaxi rides in London
briefs.summary: Fifteen Wayve-equipped electric Mustangs began carrying paying Uber riders Friday with a TfL-licensed safety driver aboard, The Register reports.

kicker: Parkersburg, Nicholas, Webster and Summers ran no regional line; nothing there cleared the 48-hour bar.

art.caption: Merchant ships at anchor off Bandar Abbas in the Strait of Hormuz, where the U.S. said Saturday it hit three Iranian tankers.
